title: Partial covering lowers the inferred W1 opacity of G2698 in eleven archived visits
abstract: We test the conversion of infrared magnitude slopes to dust opacity in Gaia DR3 2698173741829957888. The parent optical fit leaves 13.35 percent of the reference light uncovered. A curved attenuation fit to its eleven infrared and optical pairs gives a W1-to-r opacity ratio of 0.224, instead of 0.281 for a full screen. Integration over the optical errors gives 0.223. Using r data alone gives 0.227. The approximate 95 percent profile interval is 0.084-0.381 at the central covering fraction. The W2 ratio falls from 0.111 to 0.077. At a fixed size slope of 3.5, a new score for the published grain grid shifts the best graphite maximum radius from 0.849 to 0.652 um. The tested cutoff near 0.25 um still has a score loss of 6.11 for graphite and 18.45 for silicate. The correction weakens some grain-size evidence but does not remove it. Limits include eleven visits, fixed and wavelength-independent covering, approximate optical summaries, time matching, spherical grains and possible changes in infrared emission. This is a conditional reanalysis, with no new observations or ice measurement. Code, aggregate results, source hashes and an external-input retrieval script are included.
